content_voiceover: This is the European LeukemiaNet 2022 risk classification, flagged here as a must-know for boards. Favorable risk includes core-binding factor leukemias, the t 8;21 translocation with RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion and inversion 16 with CBFB-MYH11 fusion, plus NPM1 mutation without FLT3-ITD, and in-frame bZIP CEBPA mutations. Intermediate risk covers the t 9;11 translocation with MLLT3-KMT2A fusion, and critically, NPM1 mutated with FLT3-ITD, or wild-type NPM1 with FLT3-ITD, since FLT3-ITD allelic burden shifts favorable NPM1 mutants into intermediate risk. Adverse risk is the largest and most tested category: KMT2A rearrangements other than t 9;11, the t 9;22 translocation meaning BCR-ABL1, inversion 3 or t 3;3 involving GATA2 and MECOM, monosomy 5 or del 5q, monosomy 7, abnormal 17p, complex karyotype, and mutated TP53, which carries the worst prognosis regardless of other findings. The single highest-yield pearl here: NPM1 mutation is only favorable when FLT3-ITD is absent; add FLT3-ITD and it drops straight to intermediate.
keypoints: Favorable: t(8;21), inv(16), NPM1mut w/o FLT3-ITD, CEBPA bZIP
keypoint_voiceover: Remember, NPM1 without FLT3-ITD is favorable, but adding FLT3-ITD makes it intermediate. TP53 mutation and complex karyotype are always adverse, no exceptions.
